# Where the money goes: share of everyday spending by category

Files: `where_the_money_goes.pdf`, `where_the_money_goes.svg` (this file: `where_the_money_goes.md`), written by `ob_figures.py` (task T25).

**The data are synthetic.** They were generated by `ob_generator.py` from ONS averages (Family Spending, uprated), FCA Financial Lives 2024 holding rates and stated synthetic assumptions, so this figure describes the generator, not real customers.

## Source data

Source: the 100 files `Analysis/open_banking/persona*.json` (Open Banking Read/Write v3.1 objects; seed 20261107) and `Analysis/open_banking/ground_truth.csv`, written by `ob_generator.py` at commit `4287a78`; read by `ob_figures.py` (commit `unknown` or later). Plot style: `TeXFormat.py` sha256 `a33ce9f67e0a`. No random numbers are drawn here (seed: not applicable).

## Filters, transformations and units

**Everyday spending** = booked card purchases (proprietary codes `DEB` debit card and `PUR` credit card, which carry `MerchantDetails`) from every account of a person, excluding own-account transfers (any transaction whose `TransactionReference` also appears on another transaction of the same person) and excluding one-off purchases. **One-off purchases** = the annual package holiday (`JET2HOLIDAYS`) and the synthetic lumpy purchases (`CURRYS`, `KWIK FIT`, `DFS`) listed in `ground_truth.csv` (`lumpy_purchases`, matched on booking date and merchant, taking the largest amount; lumpy purchases the generator foregoes, three in all, never appear in the transactions). Pending transactions are excluded. Rent, bills, direct debits, standing orders and card repayments are committed payments and are not counted.

All 100 personas, 1 November 2025 to 31 October 2026 (12 months), summed over every person and month; share = category total
divided by the total of all categories. Other = electronics (5732), post (9402), Amazon and general retail (5999), motor repair (7538), holidays (4722). Categories are groups of merchant category codes (MCC) defined in
`ob_figures.py`. Slices are ordered by size with Other last; slices under 3% carry no label on the pie (see the table).
Amounts are in GBP; pounds are the booked `Amount`. Plotted data: [`Analysis/open_banking_figures/where_the_money_goes.csv`](../../Analysis/open_banking_figures/where_the_money_goes.csv).

## Plotted data

n = 100 personas, 52,031 booked everyday card purchases; total everyday spending GBP 784,574.36 (mean GBP 653.81 per household per month).

| Category | Total [GBP] | Share [%] | Transactions | Mean per household-month [GBP] |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Groceries | 218,024.55 | 27.79 | 16,693 | 181.69 |
| Transport and fuel | 127,688.03 | 16.27 | 9,095 | 106.41 |
| Eating out and drink | 104,117.56 | 13.27 | 8,325 | 86.76 |
| Home and DIY | 95,439.56 | 12.16 | 2,326 | 79.53 |
| Health and personal care | 69,552.34 | 8.86 | 4,601 | 57.96 |
| Leisure and entertainment | 64,704.88 | 8.25 | 5,140 | 53.92 |
| Clothing and sport | 43,058.77 | 5.49 | 2,410 | 35.88 |
| Other | 61,988.67 | 7.90 | 3,441 | 51.66 |

## Statistics

The pie and bars show shares of one pooled total; there are no error bars, tests or fits (not applicable). The one-off
purchases excluded here total GBP 128,102.48 in 192 transactions.

## Interpretation

Groceries is the largest everyday category at 27.8% of spending, followed by Transport and fuel (16.3%)
and Eating out and drink (13.3%). These shares follow from the ONS category averages and the generator's merchant
mix and are not a finding about customers.
